▪︎septic trochanteric bursitis: suspect if immunocompromised or external/puncture wound near the affected hip; hip swelling ⇡suspicion
▪︎RFs also: trauma, loss of skin integrity (atopic dermatitis, psoriasis), recent joint aspiration/inj, ♂
sig tenderness, erythema, & warmth may indicate septic bursitis
▪︎septic: acute onset, ± fever, fluctuant edema; passive joint ROM preserved if infect isolated to bursa
▪︎⇣ joint ROM → eval for concomitant septic arthritis
▪︎prepatellar/infrapatellar septic bursitis may → aseptic knee effusion (low WBC on aspirate)

» ⊕gram stain of aspirate = diagnostic of septic bursitis
▪︎eval: aspiration + XR (local trauma, osteomyelitis); fluid → Gram stain, aerobic + anaerobic cx, WBC w/ diff, crystals
▪︎septic: WBC >1,000–3,000 cells/µL; Gram stain may be ⊕ or ⊖
▪︎gold standard = bursa fluid cx (may be ⊖ d/t recent abx or fastidious organisms)
➁ intrabursal inj w/ mixture of 1%
➂ application of dry gauze w/ ACE wrap
▪︎MRSA RFs: hospitalization or surg in last 60d, LTC facility, hemodialysis, HIV
▪︎admit for IV abx + surg consult: fever >100.5°F + tachy, prosthetic joint/graft, rapid erythema progression, progression after 24h PO abx, ⇡ MRSA risk/prior MRSA, can't tolerate PO
▪︎IV: MRSA risk → vancomycin + cefazolin; MSSA/strep → cefazolin or nafcillin
▪︎initial mgnt: abx + serial eval by ortho surgeon; surgical drainage if mass effect (⇣ perfusion, compression neuropathy) or persistent sx after 36–48h abx
